claim: The applicant claimed that she would be harmed or killed by her own family and fellow villagers because she had converted to Christianity in 2009.
requested_remedy: The applicant claimed that she would be harmed or killed by her own family and fellow villagers because she had converted to Christianity in 2009.
parties: Defendant: Torture Claims Appeal Board/ Non-Refoulement Claims Petition Office

facts.F1: The applicant first arrived in Hong Kong on 7 November 2009 and was permitted to remain until 19 January 2011 or within two weeks of the contract termination whichever is the earlier.
facts.F2: The applicant's contract was prematurely terminated on 25 February 2010 but she did not leave Hong Kong on 12 March 2010 as required.
facts.F3: The applicant was arrested by the police on 6 March 2011 for overstaying.
facts.F4: The applicant lodged a non-refoulement protection claim but stopped reporting as required and was rearrested in August 2015.
facts.F5: The applicant reapplied to reopen her claim, which was rejected by the Director of Immigration on 5 February 2016 and 3 August 2017.
facts.F6: The applicant lodged an appeal/petition with the Torture Claims Appeal Board, which rejected her appeal on 29 September 2017.
facts.F7: The applicant then filed a notice of application for leave to apply for judicial review on 9 October 2017.
facts.F8: The applicant is an Indonesian national who converted to Christianity in 2009.
facts.F9: The applicant's father is a farmer and Javanese Muslim cleric in the Mosque in her home village.
facts.F10: The applicant claims that her family are religious fanatics and follow the Muslim law fanatically, believing it is a sin for a Muslim to convert to another religion and those who do must be punished and any family member who does is disowned.
facts.F11: The applicant returned home in September 2009 after her employer terminated her contract and told her family of her conversion to Christianity but hoped they would accept it and forgive her.
facts.F12: The applicant was incarcerated in a room without food and drink for days by her family but eventually left and went back to Hong Kong.
facts.F13: The applicant tried to keep in contact with her family but they refused to forgive her and told her that the villagers had said that if she came back they would burn her alive because she had disgraced the whole village and her father.
facts.F14: The applicant claims that she cannot live anywhere else in Indonesia due to a lack of family financial support nor can she live openly as a Christian because she will be harmed.
facts.F15: The Director and the adjudicator of the Torture Claims Appeal Board carefully analyzed the material, claims, and evidence in the applicant's case.
facts.F16: The applicant did not report the threats from her family and fellow villagers to the police or any authority in Indonesia.
facts.F17: The decision-makers gave sufficient reasons for rejecting all applicable grounds.

lawsuit_type: Judicial Review Application
reference_issues: Whether the Director and the adjudicator of the Torture Claims Appeal Board properly considered the applicant's evidence and Country of Origin information (COI).
Whether the Director and the adjudicator failed to consider the extended concept of State acquiescence.
Whether the Director and the adjudicator properly considered the psychological impact of the threats from the applicant's family and fellow villagers.
Whether the decision-makers gave sufficient reasons for rejecting all applicable grounds.

claim: Non-refoulement claim on the ground that he feared he would be killed by certain drug dealers after having complained to the police of drug activities in his neighborhood if he were to return to Bangladesh
requested_remedy: Non-refoulement claim on the ground that he feared he would be killed by certain drug dealers after having complained to the police of drug activities in his neighborhood if he were to return to Bangladesh

facts.F1: The applicant is a Bangladeshi man who came to Hong Kong illegally when he was arrested on 5 September 2013 and later referred to the Immigration Department on 7 September 2013.
facts.F2: He lodged his non-refoulement claim on 10 September 2013 with the Director of Immigration on the ground that he feared he would be killed by certain drug dealers after having complained to the police of drug activities in his neighborhood if he were to return to Bangladesh.
facts.F3: The applicant was born on 24 April 1991 in Bagicha, Khilgaon, Dhaka, Bangladesh.
facts.F4: He used to live with his parents in Bangladesh.
facts.F5: In 2006, while he was in his first year in university, he and his friends namely Lemon, Babu and Shuvo became concerned about illegal drug activities in their neighborhood and started investigation into the drug supply problems.
facts.F6: In June 2006 they formally filed their complaint to the Khilgaon police and provided them with the results of their investigation including the identity of three of the local drug dealers.
facts.F7: In January 2007 the applicant and his friends learnt that the three named drug dealers had been arrested by the police and became concerned for their own safety when the drug suppliers were subsequently released six months later.
facts.F8: On 8 May 2008 when the applicant met up with his three friends at the post office, he was struck on the head by someone from behind and lost consciousness.
facts.F9: On 11 May 2008 he was found lying next to a dustbin by the side of a road unconscious and was admitted to a hospital where he later woke up with a serious cut to his right eye which affected his eyesight and for which he had to wear special glasses.
facts.F10: He was told by Shuvo that they were kidnapped by those drug dealers and their gang and were interrogated and beaten by them about their complaint to the police before they were eventually released.
facts.F11: After his release from the hospital the applicant stayed away from his home village during which the drug dealers kept looking for him at his home, he therefore decided to move to Khilkhet in Dhaka City in March 2009 to avoid them.
facts.F12: There had been no further incidents until 25 August 2010 when he was told that Lemon and Babu had died from a motorcycle accident on a one-way road which caused him to suspect that those drug dealers were responsible and became concerned for his own safety again.
facts.F13: On 30 April 2011 he moved to Cox’s Bazar and worked as a junior technician at the airport.
facts.F14: About a month later he was approached by some men who offered drugs to him which he refused but when they kept pestering him, he became concerned that they may have some connection with those drug dealers back home and decided to move away to stay in his grandfather’s home in Tabaria during which there were no further incidents with the drug dealers.
facts.F15: In March 2012 the applicant left Bangladesh for China where he was accepted as a foreign student in a university in Shenyang studying aircraft maintenance and manufacturing.
facts.F16: However in November 2012 he learnt from online news that Shuvo had been murdered and called his mother in Bangladesh who advised him to stay away from the country.
facts.F17: In 2013 the applicant travelled to Xiamen and then to Shenzhen where he stayed for five months, but when he was refused his student visa he entered Hong Kong illegally when he was arrested by the police on 5 September 2013.
facts.F18: Two days later he was referred to the Immigration Department for investigation and on 10 September 2013 he lodged his non-refoulement claim on the basis that if he were to return to Bangladesh he would be killed by drug dealers as they did to his said friends, and that he would not get any protection from the police as the drug problems has spread all over the country that even some members of the parliament are involved in drug trafficking.
facts.F19: The court found that the applicant's evidence was based on hearsay and speculation.
facts.F20: The Director and Adjudicator assessed the applicant's claim on all applicable grounds, including Torture Risk, BOR 3 Risk, and Persecution Risk.

lawsuit_type: Application for Leave to Apply for Judicial Review
reference_issues: Whether the applicant has a well-founded fear of persecution by drug dealers if he returns to Bangladesh
Whether the Director and Adjudicator correctly assessed the applicant's non-refoulement claim

facts.F1: The applicant first arrived in Hong Kong on 28 July 2006 as a visitor but overstayed and was arrested by police.
facts.F2: The applicant raised a torture claim that he would be harmed or killed by three members of the rival political party Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) if he returned to Bangladesh.
facts.F3: The Director of Immigration rejected the applicant's initial torture claim, and his subsequent appeal to the Torture Claims Appeal Board was also dismissed.
facts.F4: The applicant left Hong Kong on 10 October 2011 to return to Bangladesh.
facts.F5: In or about 2013, the applicant entered Hong Kong again and made a subsequent torture claim on the same basis as before.
facts.F6: The Director regarded the applicant's subsequent claim as a subsequent claim made under section 37ZO of Part VIIC of the Immigration Ordinance, Cap 115.
facts.F7: The applicant was released on recognizance pending the Director's determination of his claim.
facts.F8: The applicant had previously been a member of the political party Awami League (AL) and had disputes with three BNP members, HD, RT, and PK, who wanted him to join their party.
facts.F9: In 2004, the applicant was arrested by police for possession of firearms and was beaten badly until a bribe was paid by his family that he was released.
facts.F10: In 2005, the applicant was assaulted by the three BNP members for refusing to leave AL to join their party, and he was hospitalized for a damaged thumb.
facts.F11: The applicant became concerned for his own safety and departed Bangladesh in July 2006 for Hong Kong.
facts.F12: Sometime in 2013, the applicant came back to Hong Kong illegally and raised a subsequent torture claim again with the Immigration Department on the same basis as before.
facts.F13: The applicant submitted additional evidence in support of his subsequent claim, including letters and documents detailing his internal relocation in Bangladesh, medical certificates, and a Chairman Certificate.
facts.F14: The Director refused to allow the applicant to make a subsequent claim under section 37ZO of the Ordinance, citing a lack of significant change of circumstances since the previous claim was determined.
facts.F15: The applicant's grounds for challenging the Director's decision were broad and vague assertions without particulars or specifics.
facts.F16: The applicant had failed to provide substantial and cogent information to show any significant change of circumstances since his previous claim
facts.F17: The applicant's subsequent claims were substantially based on the same alleged facts of threats and attacks by the same BNP supporters for his refusal to leave AL to join BNP.
facts.F18: The submitted materials presented by the applicant would not give his subsequent claim a realistic prospect of success
facts.F19: The applicant's subsequent claim contained repeated claims without merit and lack of credible new supporting evidence
